title: Mirrored canary + A/B experiments with proximity-based fallback and degradation profiles
creator: Aisha Carter
description:
Goal: deliver a robust deployment primitive that combines mirrored (shadow) canaries, controlled A/B experiments, and proximity-aware fallback across capacity tiers with defined degradation profiles and deterministic compatibility checks.

Scope:
- Mirrored canary mode that duplicates a configurable percentage of live traffic to a candidate model variant without influencing user-visible responses.
- A/B experiment primitive to split traffic deterministically (hashing by user_id/session_id) and measure quality/cost tradeoffs.
- Proximity-based routing policy that prefers regional/edge pools but can fail over to nearby regions under capacity pressure.
- Tiered degradation profiles for graceful degradation: e.g., fall back from full FP16 model -> int8 quantized variant -> cached prefix-responses -> limited-token policy.
- Compatibility scoring: static checks (tokenizer, config, output schema) and runtime signals (response shape, semantic similarity to baseline embeddings).
- Auto-rollback triggers: combined SLO/quality composite (latency P95 > SLA threshold for 5m OR error-rate > X OR embedding-drift > Y) evaluated with hysteresis windows.

Design decisions:
- Mirroring is implemented as async duplication with no added tail latency on the critical path. Mirror events feed a per-variant metrics pipeline and a shadow-eval job.
- A/B routing uses consistent hashing with tunable bucketing for deterministic exposure and easy repro.
- Proximity scoring uses weighted metric = (latency_score * 0.5 + capacity_score * 0.3 + cost_score * 0.2) and ties are broken by customer tier. We run periodic synthetic probes to update scores.
- Degradation profiles are explicit, versioned artifacts attached to a deployment. Each step is reversible and annotated with expected token-cost delta.
- Compatibility scoring returns a single 0-100 string label for now (mapped to levels: pass/warn/fail); full matrix will be in follow-up.

Telemetry and analysis:
- Mirror traffic captured to kinesis -> analytics cluster for offline QA and to the console shadow dashboard.
- A/B reports generated daily with estimated sample size, uplift/loss for quality metrics, and cost delta.
- Auto-rollback actions are logged to the deployment audit trail and emit alerts to oncall with suggested mitigation steps.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag the mirrored canary path behind enable_mirror_v2.
2) Run 1% mirror for 2 weeks against non-critical workloads and validate shadow-eval pipelines.
3) Enable deterministic A/B on internal beta customers.
4) Gate proximity fallback behind capacity-sim feature and run chaos tests (zone failures).
5) Enable auto-rollback targeting low-risk customers, then widen.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: mirror traffic volume overwhelm analytics pipeline. Mitigation: sampling + backpressure and preload schema.
- Risk: compatibility false-positive/negatives cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative thresholds + manual approval path for P0 rollouts.
- Risk: cross-region fallbacks increase cost. Mitigation: cost tagging and quota controls per customer.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEP/Mirrored+Canary+and+Proximity+Fallback
- Shadow-eval job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/shadow-eval/pull/182
- Console dashboard mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hX_sample_dash/view
- Synthetic probe runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probes/tree/feature/proximity-scorer

Next steps:
- PR for mirrored queue consumer (ENG-84120) is in review, awaiting perf signoff.
- Implement compatibility quick-check library and add to onboarding pipeline.
